reasoning: Two successful audits (deepseek-v4-flash and openrouter/free) thoroughly reviewed all 7 files and found no malicious code. The PKGBUILD downloads prebuilt binaries from official GitHub releases with proper checksums, the package() function performs standard installation operations (extracting binaries, setting SUID on Firefox sandbox helpers, installing launchers), and all other files (.install, policies.json, launcher script, desktop entry) contain only benign, expected content. The 'inconclusive' verdict from qwen3-235b was caused by HTTP 400 API errors on 4 files including the critical PKGBUILD, not by actual security concerns.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from tool failure, not substantive security analysis. Report 1 (qwen3-235b) experienced HTTP 400 BadRequestError on 4 of 7 files including PKGBUILD, preventing completion of the audit. Reports 2 and 3 successfully reviewed all files and found no issues. This is not a true disagreement about package safety but rather a coverage gap due to API failures.
coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen3-235b) failed to review PKGBUILD, README.md, policies.json, and zen-browser-twilight.desktop due to HTTP 400 API errors, leaving critical files unaudited
learnings: Implement retry logic for transient API errors (HTTP 400/500) to prevent incomplete audits
When critical files like PKGBUILD fail to audit, the tool should either retry or clearly flag the incomplete coverage rather than returning 'inconclusive'
Track and report API error rates per model to identify unreliable endpoints
Consider implementing a fallback mechanism to use a different model when the primary model experiences repeated API failures
